solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beer taken around a camp

indicators.note: the beer is wrapped around the next piece, so it goes outside

parts.note: lager is a pale beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has a beer while sitting around a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: A laager is a South African word for a camp encircled by wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is a defensive encampment, traditionally ringed with wagons.

clue.text: Spit out, then apply tongue round — to adjust this?

indicators.note: the licking word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to lick is to apply one's tongue

indicators.note: the letters of the word come out of their order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Spit, then run the tongue round the lips, as someone does when fixing their make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the scene of touching up lip colour; the definition is just its last words.
explanation.definitionFit: Licking the lips is how one evens out freshly applied lip colour, the cosmetic this question refers to.

clue.text: Flying is stunning

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on the wing, in flight

explanation.surface: Taking to the air is amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: A-wing is an old word for in flight, and awing is the participle of awe, to overwhelm.

clue.text: Milk producer breaking bottom off jug

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, and it is removed

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: Something that makes milk smashing a jug's base.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, which gives milk for cheeses such as feta.

clue.text: Brother to present with a bouquet

parts.note: Fra is the title given to an Italian friar or monk
to grant is to give or bestow

explanation.surface: A sibling hands over a gift together with a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it is the scent of a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a bouquet has a pleasant smell, which is what sweet-smelling describes.

clue.text: PC, and a different PC with no husband

indicators.note: the husband's letter is left out

parts.note: a Privy Counsellor is styled Right Hon, short for Right Honourable

explanation.surface: A police officer, and another officer who is unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: The first PC is politically correct; the second is a Privy Counsellor, entitled to be called Right Honourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is informal for holding fashionably liberal views, which is what politically correct suggests.

clue.text: Sublime swindle taking in some: don't fall into it!

parts.note: grand means splendid or sublime

indicators.note: the swindle encloses the next word

parts.note: a con is a swindle
any means some

explanation.surface: A magnificent scam that draws people in, with a warning not to be taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall into' reads as being duped by the swindle; literally it is a huge drop in Arizona.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Canyon is a vast gorge in Arizona that a visitor would not want to tumble into.

clue.text: Heavenly cake decoration left behind

indicators.note: the left letter comes after the decoration

parts.note: angelica is candied green plant stem used on cakes

explanation.surface: A divine cake topping that someone forgot to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelical is an old form of angelic, belonging to the angels of heaven.

clue.text: Old coin, one lying in the sun?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pre-decimal British sixpence
second meaning: someone getting a tan

explanation.surface: An old coin, perhaps belonging to a sunbather.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was slang for the old British sixpence coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanner was slang for a sixpenny piece, and jokingly names a sunbather who tans.

clue.text: Councillor of state that is doubly close to emperor

parts.note: 'that is' twice over: viz and ie are both short for it

indicators.note: the final letter, the one that closes the word

parts.note: the word whose closing letter is taken

explanation.surface: A state official who keeps very near to the ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz (videlicet) and ie (id est) both mean 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high minister of state in old Muslim empires, an adviser to the ruler.

clue.text: Fight here to value jewellery

parts.note: to prize something is to value it highly
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: An instruction to quarrel over how much some jewellery is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize ring is the roped arena where boxers fight for a purse.

clue.text: Have left speaking; I don't react

indicators.note: the words are to be heard said aloud rather than read

parts.note: 'are gone' means have departed

explanation.surface: Someone who has gone remarks that they are not responding.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself, a noble gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas that hardly forms chemical compounds, so it could say it doesn't react.

clue.text: Mean drunk first to be given meal outside

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: the meal word goes around the abbreviation for first

parts.note: fed means given a meal
1st, spelt IST with the digit as I

explanation.surface: A miserly drunk insists on being served first and eating outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: First is abbreviated 1ST, and the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight-fisted describes a stingy person, one who is mean with money.

clue.text: Long ribbons to wind around a legal title

indicators.note: the letters are twisted round into a new arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Lengthy strips of ribbon are coiled about a lawyer's formal title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ribbons' suggests decoration; it is pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagliatelle is pasta cut into long flat strips like ribbons.

clue.text: Solution not entirely fully explained

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, the answer sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the phrase whose letters contain the answer

explanation.surface: An answer that hasn't quite been given in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' looks like the answer to a puzzle; it is a chemical liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is an alkaline liquid, a chemical solution of potassium or sodium hydroxide.

clue.text: Dish needed by the phone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large flat plate
second meaning: the device that powers a phone's battery

explanation.surface: A plate that has to be kept by the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is an old word for a large serving platter and also a battery-charging device.

clue.text: Consciously old-fashioned sort of literary fiction?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a work rejecting the conventions of the novel

explanation.surface: A deliberately retro kind of literary novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel also means new, so the word read in two parts is opposition to the new.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-novel is experimental fiction that deliberately abandons traditional plot and character.

clue.text: Refinement of sister touring a church

indicators.note: the sister goes around the next piece, as a tourist circles a place

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun on a trip round a church shows polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle distinction, a fine shade of meaning or refinement.

clue.text: No power to take up in tired arms

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the tired word

parts.note: weary means tired

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up reads the letters upwards, in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having no energy left to lift one's weary limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' reads as limbs in the surface; it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is a collective term for weapons, which is what arms means.

clue.text: Several horses, a sort of quartet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of racehorses from one stable

explanation.surface: A team of horses described as a kind of foursome.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is a stable's set of racehorses, and string instruments make up a classical quartet.

clue.text: Scowl from unyielding champion

parts.note: grim can mean stern and unrelenting
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A frown from a stubborn sporting winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of disgust or pain, much like a scowl.

clue.text: This term, alternative to I Kings used

definitions.meaning: a phrase that stands in for the first person singular
monarchs are the ones who traditionally speak this way

explanation.surface: It reads like a note on a Bible text, an alternative version of the book of 1 Kings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I Kings' looks like the Old Testament book; split it, and I is the pronoun while kings are its users.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal 'we' is the plural pronoun a monarch uses in place of 'I'.

clue.text: Dashing knight mounted horse, holding hawk occasionally

indicators.note: the knight and horse enclose the hawk letters
in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so read upwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

indicators.note: only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the word whose alternate letters are used
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A gallant knight rides off on horseback, with a hawk on his wrist now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish means dashingly jaunty and stylish, with a hint of dissolute charm.

clue.text: Woman is pleased? Yes, extremely

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, are kept

parts.note: the word whose ends are used

explanation.surface: Asked whether a woman is happy, the answer is a firm yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladys is a woman's first name, of Welsh origin.

clue.text: Boy who's fast failing to finish

indicators.note: the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A quick lad who doesn't complete the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but it means abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard.

clue.text: Poor ruler given better brain supplement

parts.note: thin means poor or meagre
a king rules
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A weak monarch given something to boost his intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, not a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a thinking cap is the idiom for concentrating hard, so it jocularly aids the mind.

clue.text: Capital but short name for dog

indicators.note: the capital loses its last letter

parts.note: Cairo is the capital of Egypt

explanation.surface: A dog with a grand name that is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a small Scottish terrier breed, originally bred for hunting among rocks.

clue.text: Do drudgery for Dickens

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to do hack work for another, as a junior lawyer or writer
second meaning: as in 'what the dickens', a euphemism for Satan

explanation.surface: Working hard on behalf of Charles Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens' looks like the novelist but is the old mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: To devil is to do routine work for an employer, and 'the dickens' is a polite word for the Devil.

clue.text: Declaration from senator is out of order

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order, so rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A politician's statement is ruled improper in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' sounds like a parliamentary ruling but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident statement, a declaration made as fact.

clue.text: Fish picked up in this paper

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up reads the letters upwards, reversed

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish wrapped and lifted out in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a sound signal, but here the letters are lifted upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive name for a low-quality newspaper.

clue.text: Joined up and served? Not I

indicators.note: the word is used without the letter I

parts.note: soldiered means served in the army

explanation.surface: Someone enlisted and did military service, but not personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined up' reads as enlisting, which pulls toward the army; only 'Joined' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldered means fused metal parts together with molten alloy, so they are joined.

clue.text: Current year opening for information bureau

indicators.note: the current and year open up to make room for the information

parts.note: AC is alternating current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An office for news opening in the present year.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information or the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an organisation providing a service, such as a news or information bureau.
